hypothesis: The hardest soundness gap in Bloom's pipeline is NOT the proof step (ADR-006/007) but the human-language-to-predicate binding in ADR-001/003: the newest spec-synthesis work shows that even when an LLM-generated specification is machine-checkable and the implementation provably satisfies it, the specification routinely fails to capture user intent. Therefore a Bloom invariant that proves green can still encode the wrong property, and the restricted-AST readability of ADR-001 is necessary but provably insufficient as a soundness guarantee unless paired with an independent intent-conformance check (e.g. adversarial counterexample review or a spec test-vector suite).
rationale: ADR-001 bets that a readable restricted-AST predicate is arbitrable; ADR-003 binds human text to that predicate. But the frontier of LLM-driven formalization explicitly isolates 'user-intent formalization' as an UNCHECKABLE-by-construction step: 'Evaluating LLM-driven User-Intent Formalization for Verification-Aware Languages' (2024) states there is no algorithmic way to ensure the formal spec matches the informally-expressed intent, and 'Verus-SpecGym: An Agentic Environment for Evaluating Specification Autoformalization' (2026) builds a 581-task benchmark precisely because faithful spec autoformalization is an open, measured-as-failing problem. PropertyGPT (2025) and 'Extracting Formal Smart-Contract Specifications from Natural Language with LLMs' (2024) generate properties but inherit the same faithfulness gap. Readability (ADR-001) helps a human arbiter SPOT a mismatch, but the literature treats spec-intent fidelity as a distinct, unsolved verification obligation — so Bloom's seven decisions have a latent eighth: validate the predicate against intent, not just the program against the predicate.
supports_if: A controlled study (or the Verus-SpecGym / user-intent benchmarks) shows that for restricted-AST-shaped predicates, machine-checkable specs that pass verification still mis-encode the natural-language invariant at a non-trivial rate (e.g. >10%), AND that readable-AST review by humans/arbiters catches materially more of these mismatches than opaque-closure review — making the readability of ADR-001 load-bearing but only as part of an intent-conformance layer.
refutes_if: Restricting predicates to the readable, sub-Turing AST of ADR-001 is shown to drive intent-formalization error to near-zero (the restricted grammar is so simple that the human text and the predicate are isomorphic), so no separate intent-conformance check adds measurable soundness over what ADR-001/003 already provide.
motivating_papers: Evaluating LLM-driven User-Intent Formalization for Verification-Aware Languages
Verus-SpecGym: An Agentic Environment for Evaluating Specification Autoformalization
PropertyGPT: LLM-driven Formal Verification of Smart Contracts through Retrieval-Augmented Property Generation
Extracting Formal Smart-Contract Specifications from Natural Language with LLMs

hypothesis: ADR-006's source-vs-deployed-Wasm gap will close not via a heavyweight verified compiler but via lightweight, modular, per-lowering-rule translation validation — and the 2023-2026 frontier suggests Bloom should make a VERIFIED-COMPILATION-PROFILE (a validated subset of source-to-Wasm-to-native lowerings) the provenance gate, rather than treating 'verified compilation' as an all-or-nothing prerequisite. A source proof can be transported to the deployed artifact for exactly the operations whose lowering rules carry a machine-checked validation certificate.
rationale: ADR-006 correctly says a source proof does not cover deployed Wasm without verified compilation, and ADR-006/007 make proofs optional and provenance-gated. The newest work reframes 'verified compilation' from a monolith into a modular, incremental, lowering-rule-granular discipline: 'Lightweight, Modular Verification for WebAssembly-to-Native Instruction Selection' (Crocus, 2024) verifies Cranelift's individual lowering rules covering Wasm 1.0 integer ops — i.e. native codegen correctness proven rule-by-rule, not whole-compiler. 'Foundational Verification of Smart Contracts through Verified Compilation' (DeepSEA, 2024) and 'RustCompCert: A Verified and Verifying Compiler for a Sequential Subset of Rust' (2026) show end-to-end transfer is achievable only over a deliberately restricted source subset. This points at a frontier design: the provenance gate is not 'is the whole toolchain verified?' but 'does every lowering used by this petal lie inside the validated profile?' — making ADR-006's optionality concrete and the source-Wasm gap closable per-feature.
supports_if: A buildable pipeline demonstrates source-level invariant proofs transported to deployed Wasm/native artifacts soundly for the subset of operations covered by per-rule lowering validation (Crocus-style) or a restricted verified compiler (DeepSEA/RustCompCert-style), while flagging out-of-profile lowerings as unproven — and at least one historically-real miscompilation/lowering bug is caught by the rule-level certificate that source-only verification would have missed.
refutes_if: Per-rule / restricted-subset validation cannot be composed into a sound end-to-end source-to-deployed guarantee for realistic petals (composition unsoundness, uncovered lowerings dominate, or the validated subset is so small it excludes the operations petals actually need), so the only sound path remains a full verified compiler or re-execution fallback, collapsing the 'verified-compilation-profile as provenance gate' design.
motivating_papers: Lightweight, Modular Verification for WebAssembly-to-Native Instruction Selection
Foundational Verification of Smart Contracts through Verified Compilation
RustCompCert: A Verified and Verifying Compiler for a Sequential Subset of Rust

hypothesis: ADR-007's demand for a re-execution / fraud-proof fallback because of zkVM underconstraint is not just prudent but is becoming the empirically-mandated default: the newest zkVM-testing frontier shows soundness bugs (accepting invalid executions) are systematically discoverable in production zkVMs and are NOT covered by the proofs those zkVMs emit. Stronger claim: Bloom's fallback should treat the zkVM proof as a liveness/cost optimization only, never as a standalone soundness primitive, and should pair it with the SAME verified-interpreter-as-oracle pattern that already works for Wasm — i.e. a WasmRef-Isabelle-style reference oracle becomes the soundness anchor for both ADR-005 conformance and ADR-007 re-execution.
rationale: ADR-007 already hedges against zkVM underconstraint with a re-execution/fraud-proof fallback. The 2024-2026 frontier converts this hedge into a measured necessity: 'Arguzz: Testing zkVMs for Soundness and Completeness Bugs' (2025) is the first automated tool finding soundness bugs (accepting invalid executions) in real zkVMs whose constraint systems or execution logic are buggy — exactly the underconstraint failure mode — and 'SoK: What don't we know? Understanding Security Vulnerabilities in SNARKs' (2024) plus 'Towards Fuzzing Zero-Knowledge Proof Circuits' (2025) and 'Formal Verification of Zero-Knowledge Circuits' (2023) establish that 'proven secure on paper' diverges from 'sound in implementation.' Meanwhile 'WasmRef-Isabelle: A Verified Monadic Interpreter and Industrial Fuzzing Oracle for WebAssembly' (2023) shows a verified reference interpreter can serve as a deployed differential oracle in industrial CI. The frontier synthesis: a single verified-interpreter oracle can both (a) pin ADR-005 conformance and (b) be the trusted re-executor that adjudicates ADR-007 fraud proofs — unifying H4 and H6 around one trust anchor and demoting the zk proof to an optimization.
supports_if: Tools like Arguzz (or fuzzing of ZK circuits) continue to surface soundness/underconstraint bugs in deployed zkVMs at a rate high enough that an emitted proof alone cannot be relied upon, AND a verified-interpreter oracle (WasmRef-Isabelle-style) can re-execute petal transactions deterministically to adjudicate disputes — demonstrating the fallback is both necessary and constructible from the same component that backs conformance.
refutes_if: Formal verification of zk circuits (e.g. 'Formal Verification of Zero-Knowledge Circuits') matures to the point that production zkVM constraint systems are themselves machine-checked end-to-end and Arguzz-class tools stop finding soundness bugs, so a zkVM proof becomes a standalone soundness primitive and the re-execution/fraud-proof fallback of ADR-007 is redundant overhead rather than a requirement.
motivating_papers: Arguzz: Testing zkVMs for Soundness and Completeness Bugs
SoK: What don't we know? Understanding Security Vulnerabilities in SNARKs
WasmRef-Isabelle: A Verified Monadic Interpreter and Industrial Fuzzing Oracle for WebAssembly
